---
title: "KRW's race and gender report cards"
subtitle: "5.3 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Figures 7, 10A and 14"
description: "Marginal summaries and pairwise statements in the archived cards for 97 firms."
---

KRW's cards report which firms have larger contact gaps by placing firms in ordered grades. The grade assignments
and expected error rates can change with the target or the reward λ for a correct direction.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/krw-card.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["krw-card"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

Grade 1 is highest on the chosen target. The card states directions between grades and withholds them within a
grade. A correct direction earns λ, a wrong direction costs 1, and withholding pays 0. DR divides expected errors
by all pairs. E/N divides them by the number of pairs the card states.

- **Published race card.** The card states 1,324 of 4,656 pairs, with expected wrong share E/N .136.
  Its risk .1818 comprises .0387 for errors and .1431 for withholding. In this card, comparisons between distant grades have lower expected error rates than comparisons between adjacent grades.
- **Reveal grade 1.** The remaining bands stay in place. As each grade is revealed, its firms enter the disclosure
  and between-grade tables.
- **Sort by estimate.** State Farm moves 69 rows inside its grade. Changing the row order changes no reported
  direction. Genuine Parts and AutoNation illustrate why estimates alone do not determine the card.
- **λ .08: first race split.** The risk .07406 is slightly below all withheld, .07407. The extra decimal
  prevents rounding from hiding that distinction. The displayed card is still an archived KRW grid card.
- **Published gender card.** It states 731 pairs. Both ends of its signed scale are contact gaps; three stated
  directions are more likely wrong than right. The note identifies these firms and probabilities.
- **One grade.** Nothing is stated. E/N is NA: no disclosure, meaning undefined; the app draws no E/N bar.

The precision plot places each firm's original sampling SE beside its grade. The table identifies each firm.
KRW's prior depends on precision. Firms with uncertain estimates can share the middle grade while having very different contact gaps.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
KRW's code selected the grid cards using their archived probabilities and solver tolerances. The app holds those
grades fixed and evaluates them with the released postrank probabilities. The baseline race card is in Figure 7,
and the gender card is in Figure 14 (§VIII). Figures 5A and 6 are in §V.E, and Figure 10A is in §VI.B.
